context:
You picked Opus for lane sessions (item 50 b) and asked: since a lane session needs top reasoning about what it was asked, can the builder, design and other helper agents it starts run at 5.5 low effort, if anything?

What the agent files say today (read Oct 28 from agents/*.md in the repo): builders have effort high and no model set; reviewers, test authors, record writers and explorers run Haiku at very high effort; designers, design reviewers and the planner run Opus at high effort. This is from the files, not measured, and the rules' own table (agent-model-cap) may differ.

Nothing has measured whether these settings are too costly or too weak, so this is your call on direction, and the first lane to change the rules (L1) would carry it out.

options.gain: No change to what is working; no risk to checking quality.
options.how:
No change to the agent files; a later lane measures cost and quality before any change.
Before and after: the same.
options.label: Keep today's helper settings for now
options.lose: Opus lanes may spend more on helpers than they need to.

options.gain: Cheapest and fastest; the Opus lane does the thinking.
options.how:
Builders, designers and the other helpers a lane starts run Sonnet 5.5 at low effort; only the lane session itself runs Opus.
Before: mixed settings by role. After: one cheap setting for all helpers.
options.label: Helpers on Sonnet 5.5 at low effort
options.lose: Low effort may miss what a reviewer or builder should catch, and design work may get thinner.

options.gain: Cheaper than today for builders, with more care than low effort.
options.label: Helpers on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort
options.lose: Costs more than (b), and the effect on quality is still unmeasured.

ref: c201 (how the build's sessions are organized), your note on item 50 (b)
reply: Answered, Oct 28 17:50 CDT: keep today's helper settings (a). A later lane measures cost and quality before any change.
title: What model and effort should the helper agents of an Opus lane run?
why: Nothing measured shows today's settings are too costly or too weak, and a wrong cut to reviewers costs more than it saves; the L1 lane can measure first.
